claim: The official llm-d-router plugin-authoring tutorial (docs/create_new_filter.md) instructs developers to add the plugin.Register call directly inside cmd/epp/runner/runner.go's registerInTreePlugins() -- i.e. to edit the router's own repo -- as the only documented way to hook a new plugin into the scheduling flow.
stance_target: out-of-tree registration (without touching the repo) is the officially sanctioned/documented path
quoted_support: Add an import and a `plugin.Register` call in [`runner.go`](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/blob/main/cmd/epp/runner/runner.go). New plugins should generally be registered with `plugin.StabilityAlpha` unless intended to be enabled by default

claim: A minimal plugin only needs to implement plugin.Plugin (TypedName()) plus the specific interface for its plugin category (e.g. scheduling.Filter requires Filter(ctx, request, endpoints)) and a factory function of the signature func(name string, rawParameters *json.Decoder, handle plugin.Handle) (plugin.Plugin, error).
stance_target: minimum interface surface a custom plugin (including a discovery plugin) must implement

claim: After registration, a plugin is activated purely through the EndpointPickerConfig YAML: declared once in the top-level plugins list (with type, name, and optional parameters) and referenced by name (pluginRef) in a schedulingProfiles entry -- no further Go code changes needed once the factory is registered.
quoted_support:
plugins:
- type: label-selector-filter
  name: my-label-filter
  parameters:
    matchLabels:
      role: decode
schedulingProfiles:
- name: default
  plugins:
  - pluginRef: my-label-filter
